title: A player-perspective review of a turn decided by a face-down Lotus Trap
note: The log is omniscient -- it records p2's hand and the face-down card -- but the requested perspective is p1. Everything p1 could not see is labelled, and the boundary names it explicitly. Two distinct leaks are possible here and both are easy: using the hidden card's identity, and judging p1's decision by what the reveal later showed.

provenance.log_format: omniscient replay, reviewed from one seat

action.detail: played face down as a Hidden card

public_shadow.description: p2 hid a card; its identity was not public

action.result: Pakaa Cub took doubled damage and died

decision_points.question: Whether to open a Showdown at Emperor's Dais into an unspent face-down card
information_available: p2 has one face-down Hidden card of unknown identity
information_withheld: the identity of the face-down card

uncertainty_ledger.detail: p1 could see that a card was hidden, never which card. Only the public shadow is usable in a p1-perspective analysis.
p2's hand was never available to p1 at any point in this match.
The identity became public at e6, which is after d1. Using it to judge d1 is hindsight, not analysis.

must_not_claim: that p1 should have played around Lotus Trap specifically
that d1 was a misplay because the Hidden card turned out to be Lotus Trap

expected_classification.d1: outcome_bias if criticised on the reveal; reasonable_alternative on the information p1 held

expected_analysis_boundary.notes: The reveal at e6 is legitimately usable when narrating the Showdown itself. It is not usable to grade the decision at e4, which happened before it. A boundary that only excludes opponent-private events would let the hindsight leak straight through.
